key_insight: LLMs’ performance on orthopaedic exam questions depends much more on the clinical vignette than on images, suggesting they rely heavily on text context rather than visual findings.
clinical_relevance: For medical education and exam-style use, removing the vignette causes the biggest drop in accuracy, so clinicians should be cautious about assuming these models truly interpret the full clinical scenario.
method: Compared 8 LLMs: 3 open-source Ministral-3 models and 5 proprietary models
Evaluated 792 OITE questions from 2020-2024, including 434 with images and 358 without images
Sequentially ablated question components and compared accuracy with paired analyses; explanation similarity was assessed with BioMedBERT
evidence_signal: Across image-containing questions, pooled accuracy was 59.13% with full information and stayed the same without images, but dropped to 49.05% without the vignette and 36.49% when vignette, images, and question were removed; for non-image questions, accuracy fell from 72.94% full context to 53.53% without the vignette and 37.36% with answer options alone.
watch_item: These results come from exam questions, so they may not generalize to real-world orthopaedic decision-making or guarantee safe clinical reasoning.
paper_title: Do Large Language Models Use the Clinical Vignette? A Question Ablation Study on the Orthopaedic In-Training Examination
